patch_description: Instead of a causal Kalman/EMA approach, this uses a globally-applied Savitzky-Golay local polynomial (least-squares) filter, which is zero-phase: it fits low-order polynomials in a moving window and evaluates at the window's leading edge, giving trend-preserving smoothing with essentially no lag (group delay ~0) for signals well-approximated locally by cubics. Since the function receives the entire signal, we can exploit future samples within each window — unlike the causal Kalman filter which must wait for evidence and thus lags. A noise-adaptive component blends the polynomial estimate with a robust (Hampel/median) estimate to suppress outliers, and a slope-consistency pass with hysteresis eliminates spurious directional reversals. This directly targets: lag error (zero-phase fit), tracking accuracy (cubic captures sin dynamics), smoothness/slope changes (least-squares polynomial is smooth, hysteresis kills noise reversals).
